title: Schnell — a racer where nothing is modelled or textured: tracks, world, gliders and music are generated with three.js.
author: nark0se
selftext:
Schnell is a small anti-gravity racer in the browser. 

Play free: [https://deaddreamer99.itch.io/schnell](https://deaddreamer99.itch.io/schnell)

**Procedural, but steered:**

* **Tracks** are Markdown tables: one row per segment — length, turn, rise, roll, width, camera. From that the game builds the road, the gates, tunnels, colour gradients, light sweeps and even the camera moves. The code solves the last bit so every track closes on itself in 3D. The 7 story tracks are hand-tuned rows, several from my sketches.
* **A track generator** makes drafts from a seed and a few sliders (length, difficulty, curviness, hills), then lets an autopilot drive them — a draft that can't be lapped cleanly is thrown out. Drafts are a starting point; the good ones still get edited by hand. I tried a couple of alternatives, like drawing the rough outlines on the tablet, also worked quite well.
* **Music** comes from a generative 303/808/909 engine. I write patterns and steer it: tempo, mode, density, how fast the harmony moves, drum patterns, mix. One "palette" per track. The game plays 3-minute recordings of it, so it also runs on weak PCs.
* **Gliders** are small vector objects, shaped in a small editor Claude built — 8 pixel buddies, 8 gliders.
* **Size:** code, tracks and gliders together are well under 1 MB. The music recordings are the only heavy part.

The AI (mostly Claude Code, some Codex) wrote the systems. I decided what the game is: the feel, the look, every track and every palette, lots of finetuning.

\~12 days, \~31 h of active sessions.
